content.title: Matrix Addition, Subtraction, and Scalar Multiplication
content.overview: This lesson covers the fundamental operations of matrix arithmetic required for the ACT. You will learn how to perform scalar multiplication by distributing a factor to every entry and how to add or subtract matrices by combining corresponding entries.
learning_objectives: Identify the dimension requirements for matrix addition and subtraction.
Perform scalar multiplication on a matrix of any size.
Execute entrywise addition and subtraction of matrices.
Compute linear combinations of matrices (e.g., 2A - 3B) using a step-by-step process.

sections.title: The Same-Size Requirement
sections.content: Before performing addition or subtraction, you must ensure the matrices have the same dimensions (the same number of rows and columns). If Matrix A is 2x3 and Matrix B is 2x2, they cannot be added or subtracted. The resulting matrix will always have the same dimensions as the original matrices.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication
sections.content: A scalar is a single number (like 5 or -2) used to multiply a matrix. To perform scalar multiplication, multiply every single entry inside the matrix by that scalar. For example, if you multiply a matrix by 3, every number inside the brackets triples.

sections.title: Entrywise Addition and Subtraction
sections.content: Addition and subtraction are performed 'entrywise.' This means you only combine numbers that occupy the exact same position (row and column) in their respective matrices. To find the value for the top-left spot in your answer, you only look at the top-left spots of the matrices you are combining.

sections.title: The Distribute-and-Subtract Strategy
sections.content:
When faced with a complex expression like 2A - 3B, follow these steps: 1. Distribute the first scalar to all entries of Matrix A. 2. Distribute the second scalar to all entries of Matrix B. 3. Subtract the corresponding entries of the second result from the first. Always be careful with double negatives (e.g., subtracting a negative becomes addition).

![A flowchart showing the steps: Check Dimensions, Multiply by Scalars, and Combine Entrywise.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/44cad619-8237-4ef1-aec8-2153271b144c-1786505579745-218.webp)

worked_examples.question: Given Matrix A = [[1, -2], [3, 0]] and Matrix B = [[4, 1], [-1, 2]], compute 2A - 3B.
worked_examples.solution: Step 1: Multiply Matrix A by the scalar 2. 2 * [[1, -2], [3, 0]] = [[2, -4], [6, 0]]. Step 2: Multiply Matrix B by the scalar 3. 3 * [[4, 1], [-1, 2]] = [[12, 3], [-3, 6]]. Step 3: Subtract the results entrywise. Top-left: 2 - 12 = -10. Top-right: -4 - 3 = -7. Bottom-left: 6 - (-3) = 9. Bottom-right: 0 - 6 = -6. The final matrix is [[-10, -7], [9, -6]].

common_mistakes: Attempting to add or subtract matrices with different dimensions.
Only multiplying the first entry of a matrix by the scalar instead of all entries.
Sign errors when subtracting negative numbers (e.g., 5 - (-2) is 7, not 3).
Subtracting in the wrong order (B - A instead of A - B).
exam_tips: Check the dimensions first; if they don't match, the operation is undefined.
Save time by calculating just one entry (like the top-left) and checking it against the answer choices.
Watch out for 'trap' answers that have the correct numbers but the wrong signs.
content.recap: Matrix addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication are entrywise operations. Always ensure dimensions match, distribute scalars to every entry, and maintain strict attention to signs during subtraction.

knowledge_claims.content: Matrix addition and subtraction can only be performed if the matrices have identical dimensions (same number of rows and columns).
To perform scalar multiplication, multiply every individual entry in the matrix by the scalar value.
Entrywise operations mean that only the numbers in the same row and column positions are combined together.
The resulting matrix of an addition or subtraction operation will have the same dimensions as the original matrices.
A common error in matrix subtraction is failing to distribute the negative sign to every entry of the second matrix.
To quickly verify a matrix operation result, recompute a single distinctive entry, such as the top-left or bottom-right, to see if it matches the answer choice.
When calculating 2A - 3B, the correct order of operations is to perform scalar multiplication on both matrices first, then subtract the results.
Subtracting a negative entry within a matrix operation is equivalent to adding the absolute value of that entry.
If a problem asks to add a 2x2 matrix to a 2x3 matrix, the operation is impossible and the result is undefined.
In the expression kA, where k is a scalar and A is a matrix, the entry in row i, column j of the result is k multiplied by the entry in row i, column j of A.
Matrix addition is commutative (A + B = B + A), but matrix subtraction is not (A - B does not equal B - A).
Do not confuse scalar multiplication with matrix multiplication; scalar multiplication involves a single number, not another grid of numbers.

videoLesson.title: Distribute And Subtract Entrywise
videoLesson.description: Recognize how scalar factors change each matrix entry and compare corresponding entries across matrices. Multiply every entry by its scalar and subtract corresponding entries to form the result matrix.
